# AI Standard

> A security practitioner's view on using AI at work: where your data goes, what you are allowed to put in, and what the law already requires. Austria first, then the EU.

Every substantive claim carries an evidence label — Fact, Measured, Law, Assessment or Recommendation — and factual claims carry the date they were last checked against a primary source. Vendor behaviour changes without notice, so a claim here without a date should be treated as unverified.

Available in English at the paths below and in German under `/de/`.

## Start here

- [Where to start](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start): Entry points sorted by what you are allowed to decide rather than by how much you already know.
- [I am employed](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start/employee): What to find out before using AI on work material, whom to ask, and what is not yours to decide.
- [I decide for others](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start/decision-maker): The AI literacy duty under AI Act Art. 4, why shadow IT is a procurement result, and what to settle before choosing a tool.

## Data flows

- [Does the tool train on what you type?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/training-and-retention): Training is decided by the plan tier, not the vendor. Includes the trap of a developer tool on a personal account.
- [What you agree to when you allow training](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/what-you-agree-to): Allowing training is first of all allowing storage, and the two are the same switch.
- [Getting it back out](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/getting-it-back-out): Erasure requests, why EU processing is not EU jurisdiction, and where a local model genuinely fits.

## Law

- [What may go into an AI tool?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law/what-may-go-in): Personal data and confidentiality are two regimes with two different answers.
- [AI Act Article 50](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law/ai-act-transparency): Transparency and labelling duties, applicable since 2 August 2026.

## Setting up safely

- [Before you grant access](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/secure-setup/before-you-grant-access): Day-one settings, checking a directory before an agent gets it, and why a technical boundary beats an instruction in a prompt.

## Reference

- [Glossary](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/glossary): AI, data protection and tooling terms, with the confusable ones paired.
- [Documentation](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/docs): The underlying repository standard, rendered from its source.
- [Use cases](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/use-cases): Four starting points for adopting that standard.
- [About](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/about): What this site is and who maintains it.

## Optional

- [Repository](https://github.com/rubennati/ai-project-standard): The source of the standard and of this site. MIT licensed.
- [Legal notice](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/legal-notice): Operator details and licensing. Text written for this site is CC BY 4.0 — attribution required, commercial use permitted; `/docs` pages are MIT.
- [Privacy policy](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/privacy-policy): No cookies, no analytics, no third-party resources; what the hosting providers log.
